rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The audience expected swift destruction after the threat against those who denied the signs, but their prompt repentance delayed the punishment.
rows.anchor: أخبر بأنه منعهم من ذلك وحرسهم المبادرة بالتوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the narrative stresses how quickly they sinned, it puts Moses’ return and rebuke before the reason punishment was delayed and omits the acceptance of repentance mentioned in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: ولأن السياق في ذكر إسراعهم في الفسق لم يذكر قبول توبتهم كما في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom of falling into their hands pictures regret as involuntary: their teeth fall into their hands under grief and sorrow that overwhelms reflection.
rows.anchor: بعضها ندما سقوطا كأنه بغير اختيار لما غلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They recognized that they had strayed from the clear path and spoke in repentance, returning to God.
rows.anchor: قالوا } توبة ورجوعا إلى الله كما قال أبوهم آدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plea calls God the Lord whose kindness toward them has never ceased; they ask Him to sustain that kindness and erase their sins in essence and effect so He will not avenge them later.
rows.anchor: الذي لم يقط قط إحسانه عنا فكيف غضبه ويديم إحسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling themselves losers means that God would take vengeance on them for their sins.
rows.anchor: أي فينتقم من بذنوبنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses returned from intimate communion angry and sorrowful because God had informed him that his people worshipped the calf; his anger was for God.
rows.anchor: اي في حال رجوعه لما أخبره الله تعالى عنهم من عبادة العجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses calls their succession evil: they occupied his place and acted in his absence in a way that betrayed his trust.
rows.anchor: أي قمتم مقامي وفعلتم مقامي وفعلتم خلفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After me means that they worshipped other than God and failed to restrain the worshippers while Moses went to the mountain for the appointed meeting; successors should follow the one who appointed them.
rows.anchor: أي حيث عبدتم غير الله أيها العبدة

rows.speaker: الصغاني
rows.claim: Al-Saghani glosses أعجلتم as سبقتم, meaning you preceded or went ahead.
rows.anchor: قال الصغاني في المجمع : سبقتم

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another lexicographer says عجل عن الأمر means leaving an affair unfinished, while also carrying the sense of preceding.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره : عجل عن الأمر - إذا تركه غير تام , ويضمن معنى سبق

rows.speaker: أبو عبد القزاز
rows.claim: Abu ʿAbd al-Qazzaz also glosses the word as preceding someone; Ibn al-Tayyani attributes this usage to al-Asmaʿi.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أبو عبد القزاز أيضا : عجلتم : سبقتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses accuses them of assuming he had died and changing the faith as nations changed after their prophets died.
rows.anchor: فنظننتم أني مت فغيرتم كما غيرت المم بعد موت أنبيائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He threw down the Torah tablets in anger for God; this shows his anger was so intense that he could not contain himself, and that it was directed toward God's cause.
rows.anchor: أي التي فيها التوراة غضبا لله لقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses seized Aaron by the hair and dragged him to show the people how deeply he was angered by their uprooting of religion.
rows.anchor: يجره إليه } أي بناء على أنه قصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron had not failed to forbid the calf worship; invoking their mother reminded Moses of their bond and called for tenderness toward Aaron, a believer who had endured danger.
rows.anchor: ولما كان هارون عليه السلام غير مقصر في نهيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ابن أم, the vocative particle and possessive yā are omitted for brevity suited to the moment.
rows.anchor: وحذف أداة النداء وياء الإضافة لما يقتضيه الحال من الإيجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read the mīm with fatḥ, treating it like khamsata ʿashar and assuming the alif that replaces the possessive yā was deleted.
rows.anchor: وفتح الجمهور الميم تشبها له بخمسة عشر وعلى حذف الألف المبدلة من ياء لإضافة

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزه والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the mīm with kasr, on the assumption that the possessive yā was omitted for ease.
rows.anchor: وكسر الميم ابن عامر وحمزه والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم بتقدير حذف ياء افضافة تخفيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron says the people intimidated him and nearly killed him for objecting; he asks Moses not to let their enemies rejoice at his humiliation or count him among the wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: لا تسرهم بما تفعل بي فأكون ملوما منهم ومنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks forgiveness for himself for striking Aaron in anger for God's sake, and for Aaron because he had not accomplished all Moses wanted in fighting the people; he then asks for encompassing mercy, since God gives without benefit to Himself or harm from withholding.
rows.anchor: أي ما حملني عليه الغضب لك من إيقاعي باخي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since Moses and Aaron are protected from sin, the verse leaves the object of forgiveness unstated and names mercy; Moses reverses this emphasis in his later plea for himself and the seventy.
rows.anchor: طوى ما يتعلق بالمغفرة وذكر متعلق الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who took the calf as a deity will certainly receive divine wrath, a punishment that may be the order to kill themselves; it reaches them in this life and continues in the next.
rows.anchor: أي عقوبة فيها طرد أو إبعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The humiliation in worldly life repays their fabrication and also implicates those who approved their deed, especially descendants such as Qurayza, Nadir, and the people of Khaybar.
rows.anchor: أي جزاء لهم على افترائهم وكذلك من رضي فعلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recompense applies to every fabricator: anyone who transgresses through lies is humiliated, as experience shows even when some appear bold.
rows.anchor: وهذا نص في ان كل مفتر ذليل , كما هو المشاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling sins deeds indicates pardon even when people committed them knowingly; the plural stresses that no sin is too great or numerous, and ثم and من بعدها underscore repentance after time has passed.
rows.anchor: وإن أقدموا عليها على علم , وجمع إعلاما بأنه لا يتعاظمه ذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is the foundation without which deeds are not accepted; the wording makes no distinction between sins involving apostasy and other sins.
rows.anchor: على وجه يفهم أنه لا فرق بين ان يكون في السيئات ردة أو لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After repentance, God erases sins in essence and effect, however great or numerous, and treats the repentant with mercy, kindness, honor, and favor.
rows.anchor: أي محاء لذنوب الئبين عينا واثر وإن عظمت وكثرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He speculates that those who persisted in sin were the people killed when Moses ordered them to kill themselves; the survivors repented, and Aaron remained innocent at his rank of commanding right and forbidding wrong.
rows.anchor: وكأن المصرين هم الذين قتلوا لما أمرهم موسى عليه السلام بقتل أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Aaron's innocence became clear and the cause for anger disappeared, the anger ceased; سكت means it stopped, as if anger had been a speaker urging Moses until its force was spent and contentment replaced it.
rows.anchor: شبه الغضب بمتكلم كان يحث موسى عليه السلام ويعزيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anger is the heart's boiling in response to what pains the self.
rows.anchor: وهو غليان القلب بما يتأذى به النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses took up the tablets again after throwing them down.
rows.anchor: أي التي جاء بها من عند الله بعدما ألقاها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after Moses threw down the tablets, he fasted another forty days as he had for the private communion, and they were restored as two tablets in place of the broken ones.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه لما ألقاها صام - مثل ما كان صام للمناجاة - أربعين يوما أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tablets contain guidance that clarifies aims and mercy that brings honor; the people who fear their Lord alone maintain a profound fear that breaks the heart and drives them to flee.
rows.anchor: أي هم أهل لأن يخافون خوفا عظيما مقطعا للقلوب

rows.speaker: المترجم في السفر الخامس من التوراة
rows.claim: The cited Torah passage recalls Israel's forty years in the wilderness as a test and humbling, their sustenance by manna and God's word, and preserved clothes and feet; it describes the fertile land ahead and warns that prosperity can breed pride, forgetfulness, and idolatry leading to destruction.
rows.anchor: ودبركم منذ أربعين سنة في البرية ليواضعكم ويجربكم وليعلم ما في قلوبكم

rows.speaker: المترجم في السفر الخامس من التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah quotation continues by recalling Israel's stubbornness and rebellion from Egypt through Horeb, Moses' forty-day fast and the first tablets, God's threat to destroy the people, Moses' breaking the tablets and interceding, and the destruction of the calf.
rows.anchor: اذكروا ولا تنسوا أنكم أسخطتم الله ربكم في البرية منذ يوم خرجتم من أرض مصر

rows.speaker: المترجم في السفر الخامس من التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah passage continues Moses' plea on the basis of the patriarchs and Israel as God's inheritance, then recounts replacement tablets, the Ark, the Levites' service and lack of land inheritance, and exhortations to fear and obey God, remember His rescue, and care for the vulnerable.
rows.anchor: ولكن اذكر عبيدك إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Torah quotation, mouth of God is an equivocal expression that cannot be used in Islamic law and is interpreted as speech; finger of God is interpreted as power.
rows.anchor: فم الله , وإصبع الله , والأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointment returns to Moses' effort to guide Israel: by bringing the seventy to hear God's speech, he sought to move them from knowledge by inference toward direct and ultimate certainty and protect them from repeating the calf worship; their demand to see God was still disobedient.
rows.anchor: من علم اليقين إلى عين اليقين بل حق اليقين شفقة عليهم ورحمة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اختار means that Moses exerted himself to choose the best; the apposition seventy men implies others did not qualify as his people in the intended sense.
rows.anchor: أي اجتهد في أخذ الخيار { موسى قومه } ثم أبدل منهم قوله

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: The Prophet, as related by Ibn Umar and recorded by al-Bukhari and Muslim, likened people to a hundred camels among which one can hardly find a suitable mount; Biqa'i uses it to support the selection of a rare few.
rows.anchor: الناس كالإبل المائة , لا تكاد تجد فيها راحلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For our appointed time means Moses chose those he deemed fit for God's intended purpose; he and Aaron brought them near the divine address on the mountain, while Joshua ibn Nun was left over Israel by God's command.
rows.anchor: أي فما أختار إلا من رأى أنه يصلح لما نريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible construction connects the choice of the seventy to the first appointment of thirty nights in 7:142; this matches the apparent account of the Torah as discussed in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: فيكون الميقات هو الأول وهو ظلاهر التوارة كما مر بيانه في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the choice may attach to the calf episode in 7:148 or the taking of the tablets in 7:154, making this a second appointment; Aaron's presence is evidence for this reading.
rows.anchor: وحينئذ يكون هذا الميقات غير الميقات الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second-appointment reading, some of the group may have made sight of God a condition for belief, as in 2:55; this recalls the twelve scouts sent to inspect the giants, most of whom failed, and Moses feared Israel would blame him for the group's deaths.
rows.anchor: لما سمعوا كلام الله طلب بعضهم الرؤية جاعليها شرطا لإيمانهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says these seventy were different from the earlier group who demanded to see God openly and were struck by the thunderbolt; those people came before them.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما أن هؤلاء غير السبعين الذين قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quake was caused by the thunderbolt previously mentioned in al-Baqara, which shook the group and killed them.
rows.anchor: أي أخذ قهر وغلبة { الرجفة } أي التي سببتها الصاعقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative explanation is that the quake came from the divine majesty and awe they witnessed while hearing God's speech: cloud over the mountain, smoke, lightning, and horn sounds nearly shook their limbs apart.
rows.anchor: فالظاهر أن سبب الرجفة ما رأوا عند سماع الكلام من جلال الله وعظيم هيبته من الغمام الذي تغشى الجبل والقتار والبروق وأصوات القرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' question means God could have killed them and him before they reached the sacred presence, just as He could now, yet had already covered them with pardon and favor; sparing them in the holy presence is still more fitting.
rows.anchor: أي أمتهم ولما لم يكن إهلاكهم مستغرقا للماضي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the group shook because, though they disapproved of calf worship, they had failed to forbid it.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما أن رجفتهم كانت بسبب أنهم لم ينهوا عن عبادة العجل مع أنهم لم يرضوا بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says would You destroy us to speak for the whole people; he excuses them as fools and would have God forgive those who did not commit the deed directly, even if they had been silent and negligent.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما ان رجفتهم كانت بسبب أنهم لم ينهوا عن عبادة العجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If this was the later appointment after the calf episode, Moses may have feared that killing the seventy would lead Israel to disbelief, as the extra ten days in the first appointment had led them to the calf; the fools' deed could then mean calf worship.
rows.anchor: وعلى تقدير كون الميقات غير الأول يجوز أن يكون بعد اتخاذهم العجل كما تقدم عن ابن عباس
